page: OVHcloud c3-128 is a compute-optimized server instance running on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 AMD EPYC processor with 64 dedicated physical cores and 64 vCPUs, operating at a base clock speed of 2.3 GHz. The hardware configuration allocates exactly 1.0 thread per core, meaning hyperthreading is disabled. Memory capacity is 128.0 GB, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per core. Storage is provided via a bundled 400 GB NVMe SSD, and network connectivity is rated at an 8 Gbps baseline bandwidth. One complimentary public IPv4 address is included.

Benchmark results show strong multi-core performance, with stress-ng multi-core CPU and passmark CPU scores ranking in the top 10% tier. The server also demonstrates top-tier memory bandwidth for cached small blocks and strong performance for uncached large block reads and writes. Multi-threaded operations scale efficiently, as evidenced by top-tier results in bzip3 multi-threaded decompression, software compilation with Clang, ray tracing, and physics simulations. However, single-threaded performance is more moderate, with Geekbench single-core and single-threaded compression benchmarks falling in the middle 50% average tier.

This server is designed for highly parallelized workloads that benefit from dedicated physical cores without hyperthreading. Appropriate workloads include multi-threaded software compilation, ray tracing, physics simulations, and database operations, where it achieves strong Passmark database and top-tier Redis SET operation benchmarks. It also supports moderate LLM inference, processing prompts at 222.75 tokens/sec for 7B models, though text generation speeds remain in the average tier. The 2.0 GB RAM-per-core ratio represents a tradeoff, making it less suitable for memory-intensive datasets that exceed the 128 GB limit.
